idea.why: One orchestrator that synthesises and two specialists, one per source, each owning its own API tool. The sorting step the brief asks for is a first-class concern rather than an afterthought, with anti-hallucination rules at both tiers. Quibble: dashboard is read as an emailed document rather than a servable page.

structure.why: All purpose-built types with no duplication, and date windowing pushed into the tools instead of asked of the model, which is the right division. The weak point is the final hop: raw agent output goes straight into an HTML body with no parser or fence-stripping, so one markdown-wrapped reply ships as literal text.

connections.why: The wiring expresses the real dependency graph rather than a convenient line: the model fans out to all three agents, the two specialists attach as sibling tool inputs so neither fetch is serialised behind the other, and each leaf tool is scoped to its own specialist. The streams genuinely rejoin inside the orchestrator's context, which is why no Merge appears and none is needed.

answer.why: End to end it delivers and a reader would clearly recognise their request. Two shortfalls: it arrives as mail rather than something you can revisit, and the HTML has no structural guarantee behind it, only prompt instructions, so the deliverable degrades silently if the model editorialises.

appraisal: A genuinely well-shaped multi-agent briefing: an orchestrator owning synthesis and presentation, two specialists owning one source each, and leaf tools scoped to the specialist that uses them rather than hoisted to the top. The wiring is the strongest part, with a real tool fan-out and a single shared model, and time filtering done in the nodes instead of delegated to the model. The fragility is at the last hop: free-text output piped verbatim into an HTML email, so the whole deliverable rests on the model never emitting a fence. A knowledgeable user would put a guard between the orchestrator and the send.
